EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PORTABLE AP)

primary, complicated hospital course including HCAP. New fever  // Eval fever.
Eval progression of PNA

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images of the brain were obtained without

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Stationary Acquisition 5.0 s, 18.8 cm; CTDIvol = 45.5 mGy (Head) DLP =
855.5 mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Head) = 856 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  ___ CT head without contrast
___ MRI head without contrast.

FINDINGS: 

Dental amalgam streak artifact limits this study.

There are multiple areas of focal round hyperdensities scattered throughout
the cortical and subcortical brain parenchyma, some of which are associated
with surrounding areas of hypodensity, consistent with patient's known history
of multiple metastatic brain lesions and surrounding vasogenic edema.  The
surrounding vasogenic edema are most prominent in the right frontoparietal
region and the left parietal lobe.  These lesions are unchanged in size,
location and appearance when compared to ___ MRI head without
contrast and the ___ CT head without contrast.  The partially
hemorrhagic left parietal lobe lesion described in the ___ MRI is
again seen and is unchanged in appearance.  There is no evidence of interval
worsening of the left parietal hemorrhagic foci.  There are no new hyperdense
foci noted.  There is no midline shift.   The ventricles and sulci are normal
in size and configuration.

There is no evidence of fracture.  The visualized portion of the paranasal
sinuses, mastoid air cells, and middle ear cavities are clear.  The visualized
portion of the orbits are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:


1. Dental amalgam streak artifact limits this study.
2. When compared to ___ CT head without contrast and the ___ MRI head without contrast, the multiple calcified metastatic lesions, 
the right frontal parietal vasogenic edema, and the left parietal partially
hemorrhagic lesion with surrounding vasogenic edema are stable and unchanged. 
There is no evidence of acute large territory infarct or hemorrhagic
progression.  There is no midline shift.

ADDENDUM  Please note previously described clival mass is not well evaluated
on this motion degraded examination.

EXAMINATION:  MR HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ male with a history of known extensive hemorrhagic
intracranial metastatic disease, including clival mass, now with new onset
altered mental status.  Evaluate for extent of intracranial metastatic
disease.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1 weighted imaging was performed. Axial imaging was
performed with gradient echo, FLAIR, diffusion, and T2 technique were then
obtained.

COMPARISON  ___ noncontrast head CT.
___ contrast brain MRI.

FINDINGS: 

Study is severely degraded by motion, and limited due to lack of
administration interest contra.

Numerous bilateral metastatic lesions are re- demonstrated, with a dominant
partially hemorrhagic lesion within the left parietal lobe, better visualized
on the MR dated ___.  There is extensive surrounding vasogenic edema,
particularly in the right frontoparietal and left parietal lobes, which is
similar in distribution to the prior MR. ___ is also slightly increased
edema surrounding a left frontal (series 8, image 21), left parietal (see
05:15) and right frontal (see 05:17).  Grossly stable minimal bilateral
cerebellar hemisphere edema is again noted.  There is slight effacement of the
posterior horn of the left lateral ventricle, similar to ___.  No evidence
of midline shift.  Within the limitations of the examination, there is no
evidence of acute infarction.  The major intracranial flow voids are
preserved.

IMPRESSION:


1. Study is severely degraded by motion, and limited due to lack of
administration interest contrast.
2.  Within limits of study, no evidence of acute infarct.
3. Direct comparison of metastatic lesions is substantially limited secondary
to lack of intravenous contrast.  Within limits of study, left parietal blood
products versus mineralization foci are grossly similar to ___ prior
exam.
4. And within bilateral frontal, left parietal lobes and bilateral cerebellar
hemispheres.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  If clinically indicated, consider repeat examination when
patient can tolerate exam.

INDICATION:  Extensive metastatic cancer with right elbow pain.

TECHNIQUE:  Two views right elbow

FINDINGS: 

As noted on the PET-CT examination, there is a lytic lesion within the distal
humerus involving the medial epicondyle.  There is erosion of the overlying
cortex.  The finding is consistent with metastatic disease.  No definite
pathologic fracture is identified on these 2 limited views.  There is a

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with sepsis, metastatic malignancy, w/ hx of ___
s/p stenting  // Patient with ___ placed single lumen L femoral port, no blood
return, please assess ___ needle placement, also requiring more access,
please place temporary triple lumen, failed R femoral CVL at bedside X2,
___ aware and spoke with Dr. ___

COMPARISON:  Right brachiocephalic thrombectomy and SVC stenting ___

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ and Dr.
___ radiologist performed the procedure. Dr. ___
___ supervised the trainee during the key components of the procedure
and has reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA:  None.
MEDICATIONS: None.
CONTRAST: 0 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  1.3 min, 2 mGy

PROCEDURE:  PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the explanation of the risks,
benefits and alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was
obtained from the patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography
suite and placed supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was
performed per ___ protocol.  The right neck was prepped and draped in the
usual sterile fashion.
Under continuous ultrasound guidance, the patent right internal jugular vein
was compressible and accessed using a micropuncture needle. Permanent
ultrasound images were obtained before and after intravenous access, which
confirmed vein patency. Subsequently a Nitinol wire was passed into the right
atrium using fluoroscopic guidance. The needle was exchanged for a
micropuncture sheath.
The Nitinol wire was removed and a short ___ wire was advanced into the IVC.
A triple-lumen central venous catheter was advanced over the wire into the
superior vena cava with the tip in the cavoatrial junction. All 3 access ports
were aspirated, flushed and capped. The catheter was secured to the skin with
a 0 silk suture and sterile dressings were applied. Final spot fluoroscopic
image demonstrating good alignment of the catheter and no kinking. The patient
tolerated the procedure well without immediate complications.

FINDINGS: 

1.  Patent right internal jugular vein. Final fluoroscopic image showing
triple lumen central venous catheter with catheter tip terminating in the
distal superior vena cava.
2.  Left common femoral port was easily aspirated and flushed after aspiration
of the tPA dwell.  Fluoroscopy confirmed the access needle was in correct
position within the port hub.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Successful placement of a temporary triple lumen catheter via the right
internal jugular venous approach. The tip of the catheter terminates in the
distal superior vena cava. The catheter is ready for use.
2.  Functioning left CFV port.

EXAMINATION:  DUPLEX DOPP ABD/PEL PORT

INDICATION:  ___ male with septic shock and transaminitis, evaluate
for PVT or acute hepatitis

TECHNIQUE:  Gray scale, color, and spectral Doppler evaluation of the abdomen
was performed.

COMPARISON:  CTU dated ___ and MRI of the thoracic and lumbar spine
dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

Liver:  The hepatic parenchyma is within normal limits.  An 8 mm hyperechoic
lesion in the right lobe of the liver most likely represents a small hamartoma
based on the appearance of the recent thoracic spine MRI.  There is no
ascites.
Bile ducts:  There is no intrahepatic biliary ductal dilation.  The common
hepatic duct measures 7 mm.
Gallbladder:  The gallbladder is moderately distended but otherwise appears
within normal limits, without stones, abnormal wall thickening, or edema.
Pancreas:  The imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits,
with portions of the pancreatic tail obscured by overlying bowel gas.
Spleen:  The spleen demonstrates normal echotexture, and measures 9.6 cm.
Kidneys:  The right kidney is not well-visualized.  The left kidney measures
8.8 cm.  No stones, masses, or hydronephrosis are identified in either kidney.

Doppler evaluation:
The main portal vein is patent, with flow in the appropriate direction.
Main portal vein velocity is 37 cm/sec.
Right and left portal veins are patent, with antegrade flow.

The main hepatic artery is patent, with appropriate waveform.
Right, middle and left hepatic veins are patent, with appropriate waveforms.


IMPRESSION:


1. Patent hepatic vasculature.
2. Distended gallbladder without secondary signs to suggest cholecystitis.
3. 8 mm hyperechoic right hepatic lesion likely a small hamartoma based on
prior MRI.  Numerous additional small lesions are not visualized on the
present study.

EXAMINATION:  PAROTID US

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with h/o adenocarcinoma and parotitis of lung now
with pericarditis, evaluate for parotitis appear

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale with color and spectral Doppler ultrasound of the
parotid glands bilaterally was performed with a linear transducer.

COMPARISON:  CT of the neck dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

The right parotid measures: 3.1 x 1.1 x 4.0 cm.
The left parotid measures:  2.9 x 1.5 x 4.7 cm.

The parotid echogenicity is normal, without focal abnormalities.
Vascularity is normal and symmetric.

IMPRESSION: 

No significant edema or hyperemia of either parotid gland.  The left gland
measures minimally larger than the right.  Previously seen parotitis appears
to have resolved.
